name: Neural execution of graph algorithms (MPNN-max executor)
q1_graph: Encode-process-decode MPNN over the input graph; processor applied per algorithm step; learned termination network.
q4_state_persists: Yes: latent node states carried across algorithm steps.
q5_weight_sharing: Processor shared across steps and nodes.
q6_training: Supervised on every intermediate algorithm step (hints) plus termination.
q8_stability: Mean aggregation collapses OOD (21.40% at 100 nodes); max aggregation stable.
q10_more_iterations_help: Learned halt capped at |V| steps; iteration count tied to algorithm.
q13_best_results: Reachability last-step 99.80% at 100 nodes (MPNN-max) vs 91.51% GAT-full; unmatched params/FLOPs.
q14_unexplored: No looped-Transformer baseline at matched compute; no learned edges.

name: CLRS-30 baselines (MPNN, PGN, GAT, Memnet, Deep Sets)
q1_graph: Encode-process-decode GNN over a fully connected graph plus input graph, one processor step per hint step.
q2_edges: Fixed (fully connected execution model); PGN adds supervised pointer edges.
q6_training: Hint-supervised teacher-forced rollouts; JAX/Haiku.
q8_stability: Overfitting to training size: MPNN in-distribution gains do not transfer to 4x graphs.
q13_best_results: OOD average micro-F1: MPNN 44.99%, PGN 50.84%; strings ~3%. Unmatched FLOPs.
q14_unexplored: No looped-Transformer arm; test ladder only 4x.

name: Triplet-GMPNN (generalist neural algorithmic learner)
q1_graph: Gated MPNN on fully connected graph with triplet (node-node-node) messages max-reduced into edge latents.
q2_edges: Fixed graph; edge latents updated each step.
q3_topology_at_inference: No (edge states change, connectivity does not).
q4_state_persists: Yes, node and edge latents persist.
q5_weight_sharing: Single processor shared across steps and 30 tasks.
q6_training: Hint-supervised; per-node update gate.
q7_scaling: Triplet messages are cubic in nodes per step.
q8_stability: Gate stabilises single-task learning; no gain multi-task.
q13_best_results: CLRS-30 OOD average 74.14%; only 11/30 algorithms above 90%; Quickselect 0.47%. Unmatched params/FLOPs.
q14_unexplored: Edge creation instead of dense triplets; matched comparison with looped Transformer.

name: Pointer Graph Networks
q1_graph: GNN over input set/graph plus one inferred pointer edge per node, then message passing over pointers.
q2_edges: Learned per step via pointer prediction.
q6_training: Pointers directly supervised from data-structure traces (DSU, link/cut trees).
q9_capacity: Linear number of pointer edges keeps graph sparse.
q13_best_results: 5x larger test inputs on dynamic connectivity, beating unrestricted GNNs and Deep Sets; unmatched.
q14_unexplored: Unsupervised pointer/edge discovery; top-k>1 pointers; comparison vs Transformers.

name: Neural Execution Engines
q1_graph: Transformer subroutine with learned conditional mask; predicted pointer modifies the mask at next invocation.
q4_state_persists: Yes, via mask and pointer state.
q6_training: Subroutine-level supervision; binary number encodings.
q8_stability: Plain Transformer attention entropy rises with length (fuzzy attention).
q13_best_results: Sorting length 100 near-perfect after training on <=8 (selection/merge sort).
q14_unexplored: End-to-end training without subroutine supervision.

name: Deep Thinking nets / DT-Recall
q1_graph: Weight-tied convolutional recurrent block on a grid; input re-injected each iteration (recall); readout head.
q4_state_persists: Yes, latent grid state across iterations.
q6_training: BPTT with progressive loss over random iteration counts (at most 30 training iterations for prefix sums).
q7_scaling: Prefix sums 32-bit to 512-bit; mazes 9x9 to 59x59 and larger.
q8_stability: Overthinking (degeneration when iterated far); fixed by recall + progressive loss.
q9_capacity: Recurrent nets emulate deeper feed-forward nets with fewer parameters.
q10_more_iterations_help: Yes, far beyond training horizon: 237 iterations (prefix) and 984 (mazes) at peak.
q13_best_results: 512-bit prefix 97.12%; 59x59 mazes 97.30%; chess 82.69% vs FF 61.17%. Depth-matched, not FLOP-matched.
q14_unexplored: Graph (non-grid) substrate; learned topology; matched looped-Transformer comparison.

name: Maze logical-extrapolation critique (DT-Net, PI-Net)
q1_graph: Pretrained DT-Net (recurrent CNN) and PI-Net (implicit/DEQ) maze solvers.
q6_training: Pretrained models re-evaluated; PI-Net uses Broyden solver.
q7_scaling: Maze size, percolation and deadend-start axes varied.
q8_stability: Limit cycles in non-fixed-point models; PI-Net needs Broyden threshold 1000.
q10_more_iterations_help: Not for cycles: outputs unchanged by extra iterations once percolation > 0.
q11_gpu: PI-Net solver memory scales with Broyden threshold.
q13_best_results: DT-Net matches deadend-filling on 98.8% of 143k mazes; fails when mazes contain loops.
q14_unexplored: Training distributions that force general shortest-path algorithms.

name: SALSA-CLRS sparse baselines (GIN(E), PGN, RecGNN)
q1_graph: Sparse message passing over the input graph only.
q6_training: Trained n<=16 ER graphs without hints.
q7_scaling: Tested up to n=1600 (100x) across ER, WS, Delaunay.
q11_gpu: Sparse execution avoids CLRS OOM; PyTorch + PyG.
q13_best_results: BFS RecGNN 99.2% node acc at n=1600 ER but 55.6% Delaunay; DFS fails; Eccentricity graph-acc to 0%.
q14_unexplored: Learned edges and Transformer baselines on SALSA.

name: Recurrent NAR (LSTM aggregator)
q1_graph: Triplet-GMPNN-style processor with LSTM aggregation over ordered neighbours.
q6_training: Hint-supervised CLRS.
q13_best_results: Quickselect 87% micro-F1 vs 0.47% for Triplet-GMPNN; same architecture except aggregator.
q14_unexplored: Order-sensitive aggregation inside a recurrent graph substrate.

name: Discrete NAR / no-hint NAR / Hint-ReLIC (supervision variants)
q1_graph: GNN processors with discrete state bottlenecks (DNAR) or self-supervised regularisers (no-hint, Hint-ReLIC).
q6_training: DNAR: state-transition supervision; no-hint: final-output only plus regulariser; Hint-ReLIC: causal augmentation.
q13_best_results: DNAR perfect test scores; no-hint sorting 98.7% vs 95.2%; Hint-ReLIC up to 3x OOD.
q14_unexplored: Whether such guarantees survive without algorithm-specific supervision.

name: ForgetNet / G-ForgetNet
q1_graph: CLRS processor without historical embeddings (Markov step); G-ForgetNet gates history back in.
q6_training: Hint-supervised.
q8_stability: History removal hurts early training, motivating the gate.
q13_best_results: unknown
q14_unexplored: Persistent state vs Markov state under free (unsupervised) latent dynamics.

name: Relational Transformer
q1_graph: Transformer attention over all node pairs that also reads and updates edge vectors each layer.
q6_training: CLRS hint training with tuned hyperparameters.
q13_best_results: CLRS OOD average 66.60% vs MPNN 49.23%; plain Transformer 42.34% vs RT 81.30% on 8 core tasks. Not param-matched.
q14_unexplored: Looped (weight-shared) RT on large-size ladders.

name: Looped Transformer simulating graph algorithms
q1_graph: Looped Transformer block with extra attention heads that read the adjacency matrix.
q2_edges: Given input graph via attention heads.
q6_training: Existence by construction (no training).
q7_scaling: Parameters independent of graph size; precision limits node count.
q8_stability: Finite precision limits simulable graph size.
q9_capacity: Constant parameters for any graph size (up to precision).
q13_best_results: Theorem: 17-layer, 3-head O(1)-width block simulates Dijkstra.
q14_unexplored: Learnability of these constructions from data.

name: Recurrent Relational Network (Sudoku)
q1_graph: 81 cell nodes, edges within row/column/box, shared MLP message and LSTM-style update, readout every node every step.
q6_training: Loss at every step (deep supervision), 32 training steps.
q10_more_iterations_help: Yes: trained 32 steps, run 64 at test, 17-given accuracy rises to 96.6%.
q13_best_results: 96.6% on 17-given Sudokus; baselines are other solvers, unmatched.
q14_unexplored: Learned (non-given) constraint edges; size-scaled Sudoku (16x16).

name: Discovering Neural Wirings
q1_graph: Channels as nodes in a general graph; static (acyclic) or dynamic (cyclic, time-varying state) neural graphs.
q2_edges: Learned during training (edge weights swap in/out).
q3_topology_at_inference: No: learned once, fixed after training.
q6_training: Joint weight and wiring learning in one training run.
q13_best_results: +10% ImageNet for MobileNetV1 at ~41M FLOPs (FLOP-matched).
q14_unexplored: Per-input or per-iteration wiring; reasoning tasks.

name: Dynamic sparse training (SET, RigL, Top-KAST)
q1_graph: Sparse layers in standard feed-forward nets.
q2_edges: Learned during training: drop by magnitude, regrow by gradient (RigL) or randomly (SET).
q6_training: Standard SGD with periodic topology updates; Top-KAST never computes dense gradients.
q7_scaling: Fixed parameter count and compute throughout training.
q9_capacity: SET: quadratically fewer parameters without accuracy loss (authors).
q13_best_results: RigL ResNet-50 96.5% sparse: 72.75% top-1.
q14_unexplored: Topology updated per input or per inference step.

name: Random / weight-agnostic topologies (RandWire, WANN)
q1_graph: Networks wired by random graph generators (RandWire) or searched topologies with one shared weight (WANN).
q6_training: RandWire: standard training; WANN: architecture search.
q13_best_results: Random generators give competitive ImageNet accuracy.
q14_unexplored: Random-sparse control for learned-topology claims on reasoning.

name: Recurrent Independent Mechanisms
q1_graph: k_T recurrent modules; input attention activates top-k_A; active modules communicate via key-value attention.
q3_topology_at_inference: Yes: active set chosen per step from state and input.
q6_training: BPTT.
q13_best_results: Copying train 50/test 200 CE 0.00 vs Transformer 0.54; seq-MNIST 24x24 38.1% vs LSTM 21.9%.
q14_unexplored: Algorithmic size extrapolation; shared-weight modules.

name: Neural Production Systems
q1_graph: Entity slots plus a set of rule templates; best-matching (rule, slot) pairs selected and applied.
q3_topology_at_inference: Yes: sparse rule-entity bindings each step.
q6_training: unknown
q13_best_results: unknown
q14_unexplored: Algorithmic benchmarks with size extrapolation.

name: Shared Global Workspace
q1_graph: Specialist modules write to and read from a limited-capacity shared workspace (hub).
q6_training: unknown
q9_capacity: Capacity limits argued to encourage specialisation.
q13_best_results: unknown
q14_unexplored: Workspace as hyperedge vs sparse pairwise edges on algorithmic tasks.

name: Cannistraci-Hebb brain-inspired dynamic sparse training
q1_graph: Ultra-sparse MLP/Transformer layers initialised with bipartite receptive-field network model.
q2_edges: Gradient-free topology-driven link regrowth during training.
q6_training: Dynamic sparse training with density decay.
q7_scaling: Earlier CHT was O(N d^3); GPU matrix approximation introduced.
q9_capacity: 5% connections beat dense on two MT tasks (authors).
q13_best_results: Outperforms dense Transformers on two translation tasks at 5% connectivity; not param-matched.
q14_unexplored: Recurrent use; reasoning tasks.

name: Resonant Sparse Geometry Networks
q1_graph: Nodes in learned hyperbolic space; input-dependent sparse connections decaying with geodesic distance.
q6_training: Two-timescale learning incl. Hebbian.
q9_capacity: Claims 15x fewer parameters than Transformers on long-range task.
q13_best_results: Hierarchical 20-class: 23.8% (41,672 params) vs Transformer 30.1% (403,348); unmatched.
q14_unexplored: Independent replication; matched comparison.

name: Continuous Thought Machine
q1_graph: Neurons with private history-processing weights; synchronisation matrix as latent; internal ticks.
q6_training: unknown
q13_best_results: unknown
q14_unexplored: Matched comparison to looped Transformer on extrapolation ladders.

name: HRM / TRM recursive reasoners (benchmark-level view)
q1_graph: Tiny 2-layer network applied recursively to latent and answer states with deep supervision and ACT.
q6_training: Deep supervision over up to 16 supervision steps; ACT halting.
q8_stability: No guarantee HRM reaches a fixed point.
q10_more_iterations_help: ARC: most accuracy at first recursion step; HRM gains come from training-time refinement.
q13_best_results: Sudoku-Extreme 87.4% (MLP), Maze-Hard 85.3%, ARC-AGI-1 44.6%; same-size Transformer within ~5pp of HRM.
q14_unexplored: Size extrapolation (tasks are fixed-size).
